citations.narrative:
The facility does not have a current record of animals on hand. The records are missing a total number of animals and
animals that have been born/euthanized since the last inspection. Improper recordkeeping does not allow APHIS officials
to properly account for animals on the premises or allow for proper tracking of animals. Each dealer and exhibitor shall
make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose all information required by the AWA
concerning each animal purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, or otherwise in his or her possession or under his
or her control, or which is transported, euthanized, sold, or otherwise disposed of by that dealer or exhibitor. Correct by
ensuring there is a complete and appropriate record of animals on hand.

A strong odor of ammonia is present in the animal housing areas. The inspectors' eyes felt irritated throughout the
inspection of the building. The licensee stated that cleaning in the different rooms have ranged in cleaning from one to two
weeks. High levels of ammonia can cause discomfort to the animals and lead to further health issues.
Indoor housing facilities shall be adequately ventilated by natural or mechanical means to provide for the health and to
prevent discomfort of the animals at all times. Such facilities shall be provided with fresh air either by means of windows,
doors, vents, fans, or air-conditioning and shall be ventilated so as to minimize drafts, odors, and moisture condensation.
The licensee must ensure that the ammonia is kept at a compliant level either by removal of ammonia causing waste
and/or proper ventilation at all times in order to support the health of the animals. Correct by, 16-June-2026.

The food provided in two enclosures housing two chinchillas is not wholesome and palatable. The food that is typically a
light brown/green pellets have become dried and dark grey. There is also a white dusty material present on the pellets.
Failure to provide wholesome and palatable food to animals can result in malnutrition, exposure to contaminates (mold),
and disease. Correct by ensuring that the food is wholesome, palatable, and free from contamination and of sufficient
quantity and nutritive value to maintain all animals in good health. The diet shall be prepared with consideration for the
age, species, condition, size, and type of the animal. Animals shall be fed at least once a day except as dictated by
hibernation, veterinary treatment, normal fasts, or other professionally accepted practices. Correct by, 11-June-2026.

The facility is not adequately cleaning the premises. In the building housing the chinchillas there is an excess of discarded
bedding and fecal material on the floors between the rows of animal enclosures. There are numerous cobwebs observed
throughout the facility including on top of and behind the enclosures currently housing animals. Multiple enclosures were
observed with clumps of hair from the animals trapped in the wire fencing in both the front and rear of the enclosures. Hair
was also seen caught between the stacked enclosures and on the automatic watering lines. The enclosures that utilize
pull-out trays to catch animal droppings were observed excessively full of feces, urine, bedding, and food. These pull-out
trays vary in severity with multiple trays observed with moldy and decomposing dark brown/black organic material with
numerous flies swarming out of the trays.
Failure to adequately clean the animal enclosures and the premises can lead to illness, transmission of diseases, and
attract unwanted pests. The facility must ensure that the premises are kept clean and in good repair to protect the animals
from injury to facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.

An effective pest control method was not being utilized by the facility. Excessive flying insects were noted in enclosures in
the back room of the facility housing chinchillas. When the chinchilla enclosure was touched, a large swarm of insects
was observed within and around the enclosure. Insects can spread disease, contaminate food and water, and cause
discomfort and distress to the animals. A safe and effective program for the control of insects and pests must be
established and maintained. The licensee must establish an effective plan for the control of the insects. Correct by 16-
June-2026.
This is a continuation of the report for the routine inspection conducted 09-June-2026 and contains the remaining non-
compliances found during the inspection. The exit briefing for the items included on this report was conducted on 11-June-
2026.
This inspection was conducted with the Facility Representative on 09-June-2026. The exit interview was conducted with
the Facility Representative on 11-June-2026.
Additional Inspectors:
Eric Irvin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
